title: Select
description: Select handles single and multi-select choices from predefined options. It supports searchable lists, clear actions, custom item templates, and shared field states for form and filter workflows.
intro: Select is appropriate when users choose from a bounded set rather than entering freeform text. It covers multi-select with comma-separated trigger text, client-side search, custom item presentation, and reactive forms integration without async data loading complexity.

featureSections.title: Basic single select
featureSections.description: Start with a stable option set, a clear label, and helpful placeholder or helper text only when they reduce ambiguity rather than repeat the label.

featureSections.title: Variants, sizes, and field states
featureSections.description: Select inherits the shared field shell, so visual variants, density, required styling, readonly, and disabled states should look consistent with the rest of the form system.

featureSections.title: Multi-select
featureSections.description: Use multi mode when the list represents a set of filters or recipients. Selected labels appear as comma-separated text in the trigger to avoid wrapping issues.

featureSections.title: Search, clear, and disabled options
featureSections.description: Searchable and clearable affordances matter most when the option set is long enough to justify them. Disabled items stay visible for context but are skipped by keyboard and selection logic.

featureSections.title: Custom item template
featureSections.description: Some select choices need more than a single label. A projected item template can add secondary metadata or richer layout while the component still owns keyboard, focus, and selection behavior.

featureSections.title: Form composition
featureSections.description: Show select as part of a real workflow, mixing single and multi-select fields with actions and a compact state summary so the example is reusable instead of purely illustrative.

accessibility.title: Accessible name and role
accessibility.body:
The trigger uses `ariaLabel` when provided and otherwise falls back to the visible `label`.

| Mode / input | Exposed semantics |
| --- | --- |
| `single` | `combobox` trigger controlling a `listbox` |
| `multi` | `listbox` trigger with `aria-multiselectable="true"` |
| `ariaLabel` | explicit accessible name override |
| visible `label` | default accessible name fallback |

accessibility.title: Keyboard model
accessibility.body:
Disabled items are skipped during navigation.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | opens the panel and moves highlight through selectable items |
| `Home` / `End` | jumps to the first or last selectable item |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | moves through longer lists in larger steps |
| `Enter` / `Space` | selects the highlighted option |
| `Escape` | closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger |
| `Tab` | leaves the control and closes the panel |

accessibility.title: Active descendant and selection state
accessibility.body:
The component tracks the active option through `aria-activedescendant`. In multi-select mode, the trigger text is a sighted summary; the authoritative accessibility state remains on the trigger and list options.

| Input / state | Attribute |
| --- | --- |
| active option | `aria-activedescendant` |
| open state | `aria-expanded` |
| controlled panel | `aria-controls` |
| selected option | `aria-selected` on each option |
| disabled option | `aria-disabled` on each option |

apiSections.title: SelectComponent - ui-select
apiSections.lead: Standalone select field built on the shared FieldComponent. It supports single and multi-select flows, projected item templates, and integrates with Angular forms through ControlValueAccessor.

paragraphs: Projected item content is supported through an ng-template named itemTemplate.
Multi-select uses comma-separated labels in the trigger and checkboxes in the panel; single-select uses a checkmark in the panel.
The component implements ControlValueAccessor, so it works with ngModel and reactive forms.
